sophia: FYI nightly-evals flagged a big regression on legal-summaries promptset for redwood-xl-1.2b-int8, hallucination rate jumped from 3.1% -> 9.3%
sophia: failing tests mostly are structured bullet summaries — outputs inventing case citations or adding extra clauses
sophia: job: nightly-eval/2322-legal-run, commit: a1b2c3d4, quant-profile: qp-int8-v5
sophia: attaching small reproducer below
```
python tools/run_eval.py --model redwood-xl-1.2b-int8 --promptset prompts/legal-summaries/seed-42.json --seed 42 --save outputs/regress-demo.json
```
Ravi: looking now — can reproduce locally with that prompt file
Ravi: quick diff of top-level metrics:
- rougeL: 0.78 -> 0.66
- hallucination_rate (detected by eval heuristics): 0.031 -> 0.093
Marta: I ran a token-level alignment on a few examples, noticed premature token dropping after long parentheticals like "(see sec. 4.2)"
Marta: sample before (fp16): "...as shown in Smith v. Jones (2018) the court ruled..."
Marta: sample after (int8 qp-v5): "...as shown in Smith v. Jones"
Luis: that sounds like an attention masking / pad handling bug where trailing tokens are truncated during KV replay
Luis: suspicious change: commit that introduced packed-sparse-attn micro-optimizations merged in qp-v5 build pipeline (build 2023-11-08-qpv5)
Ravi: I dumped KV cache lengths during generation; with fp16 KV lengths grow as expected, int8 qp-v5 shows an off-by-one in the attention index for sequences with parentheses and line breaks
Ravi: log snippet:
```
# generation state (truncated)
step 45: kv_len=46
step 46: kv_len=47
step 47: kv_len=46  # unexpected shrink
```
sophia: good find. hypothesis: packed sparse attention kernel + quantized weights + our tiled KV packing produce an index underflow for certain token boundary tokens (parens/newlines)
Marta: seems plausible — those boundary tokens change tokenization length distribution, causing a different packing path in the quant runtime
Marta: repro matrix: only triggers when (1) quant profile qp-int8-v5, (2) packed-sparse-attn enabled, (3) input has nested parentheses or multi-line bullets
Luis: P0 mitigation proposal: immediate rollback of qp-int8-v5 for hosted model tags -> revert to qp-int8-v4 and gate builds that use packed-sparse-attn with qp-int8-v5
Luis: P1 medium: deploy canary rollback to 10% traffic and run expanded evals including nested-paren prompts and code-block style prompts for 48h
Ravi: Suggested gating rule: block any quant/profile build where nightly-eval delta(hallucination_rate) > 1.5% absolute vs baseline across critical promptsets (legal, finance, qa)
Marta: infra action: add a targeted unit test in runtime that simulates KV packing for boundary tokens (parens/newline) and checks kv_len monotonicity during decode
Marta: PR to add unit test linked: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/6421 (WIP)
sophia: owners + deadlines:
- Luis: rollback qp-int8-v5 on hosted tags (ETA 1h)
- Ravi: run 48h canary and extended evals (ETA 48h)
- Marta: add unit test + small reproducer in runtime repo (ETA EOD)
sophia: also adding a short-term alert for nightly-eval if hallucination_rate increases by >2% in any promptset until this is closed :eyes:
eng-ml-bot: deploy rollback job started: job_id=deploy-rollback-2322-001, status=queued
Luis: rolled back hosted tag to qp-int8-v4 for redwood-xl-1.2b-int8 (deployed to hosted, canary disabled) :white_check_mark:
Ravi: running extended eval now, kicking off 3 runs with different seeds (42, 101, 7)
Ravi: initial canary numbers look promising — hallucination_rate back to ~3.4% on small sample
Marta: opened runtime PR for packed-sparse-attn guard, added KV monotonicity assert and small fuzz test (PR 6421)
Marta: request reviews from @Luis and @sophia
sophia: next steps:
- monitor nightly-eval and canary results for 72h
- keep qp-int8-v5 gated until runtime fix + quant profile re-calibration and full evals
- add gating rule to CI for future quant/profile merges
